events.text: The Red Thread Elder leaves you in a pavilion where the Cloud-Weaver House spins the weather of the eastern isles. {npc} does not look up from the loom. {He} weaves a small cloud in the shape of your face, frowns at it, and unpicks the nose.

choices.text: Compose a verse about the cloud

mem.note: made a verse about my cloud

ok.log: {npc} stops weaving. The next cloud {he} makes is a perfect likeness, and {he} gives it to you.

mem.note: made a bad verse about my cloud

fail.log: The verse is not good. {npc} laughs, which is better than nothing, possibly.

choices.text: Praise the weaving honestly

mem.note: praised my weaving honestly

effects.log: "The nose was right the first time," you say. {npc} puts it back, and looks at you properly.

choices.text: Ask {him} to teach you a single thread of it

mem.note: wanted to learn the loom

effects.log: You spend the afternoon learning to make a thread of mist. It falls apart. {He} says that is how everyone begins.

events.text: {npc} of the House of the Frost Moon receives you in a hall of carved ice, seated, and does not offer you a chair. "Everyone who comes here wants our seat at the Jade Court," {he} says. "Which are you?"

choices.text: Say you came for {him}, not the seat

mem.note: said it came for me, not the seat

effects.log: A long silence. Then a servant brings you a chair, which in this house is very nearly a declaration.

choices.text: Be honest: the seat matters too

mem.note: admitted wanting our seat

effects.log: "At least you do not lie," {npc} says, coldly pleased. Word of your frankness goes round the Jade Court within a day.

choices.text: Leave a frost flower on the arm of {his} seat and go

mem.note: left a frost flower and went

effects.log: You leave without a word. The next morning a frost flower is waiting on your own doorstep.

events.text: On the observation terrace of the Pavilion of Falling Stars, {npc} tells you within the first minute that the stars have no will, that fate is only arithmetic, and that you are welcome to disagree if you can.

choices.text: Disagree, and argue it through the night

mem.note: argued the stars with me all night

ok.log: By dawn neither of you has won, and {npc} says it is the best night {he} has had in a century.

mem.note: lost an argument about the stars to me

fail.log: {He} takes your argument apart star by star, kindly. You learn a great deal.

choices.text: Say nothing, and watch the stars with {him}

mem.note: watched the stars with me in silence

effects.log: A star falls at midnight. Neither of you says anything about it. That seems, somehow, to settle something.

choices.text: Ask what arithmetic says about the two of you

mem.note: asked what the stars said of us

effects.log: {npc} actually works it out, on a slate, very seriously. {He} will not tell you the answer.

events.text: The Vermilion Phoenix House receives you with a feast of absurd luxury: rivers of wine, peaches older than empires, a phoenix feather in every cup. {npc} says very little and watches what your eyes rest on.

choices.text: Look only at {npc}

mem.note: looked at me and not the treasure

effects.log: Halfway through the feast {npc} leans over and says, "You are the first one who has not priced the cups." You did not know it was a test.

choices.text: Praise every treasure, as good manners ask

mem.note: praised our treasures

effects.log: The house is pleased. {npc} is polite. You have the feeling you have answered the wrong question very well.

choices.text: Give {him} a plain cup made by a mortal potter

mem.note: gave me a mortal potter's cup

effects.log: {npc} turns the clumsy cup in {his} hands for a long time, and drinks from it for the rest of the feast.

events.text: On the highest of the Nine Peaks, with the wind tearing at both of you, {npc} raises {his} fists and grins. "My house marries level or up," {he} says. "Show me which you are."

choices.text: Fight {him} with everything you have

mem.note: fought me with everything on the peak

effects.log: The peak loses its top. You both lie in the rubble afterwards, bleeding a little, laughing a great deal.

choices.text: Let {him} win, gracefully

mem.note: let me win on the peak

effects.log: {He} knows at once. "Never do that again," {he} says, and is not entirely angry.

choices.text: Decline: you fight enemies, not suitors

mem.note: would not fight me on the peak

effects.log: {npc} lowers {his} fists slowly, and looks at you as if seeing you for the first time.

events.text: The House of the Silent Bell keeps the temple of heaven, where no word has been spoken in nine thousand years. {npc} leads you inside, sits, and looks at you. The meeting, it seems, will be silent.

choices.text: Keep the silence the whole day

mem.note: kept the silence with me all day

effects.log: At sunset {npc} stands, bows, and touches your sleeve once. In this house that is a great deal.

choices.text: Write {him} a note instead of speaking

mem.note: wrote to me in the temple

effects.log: {He} reads it, writes an answer, and by sunset you have filled a whole scroll between you without a sound.

choices.text: Speak, softly, because you must

mem.note: spoke in the temple of heaven

effects.log: Your voice is the first in nine thousand years. Every head in the temple turns. {npc} hides a smile behind {his} sleeve.

events.text: The Thunder Gate House keeps the storm gates at the edge of the sky. {npc} meets you on the gate itself, in the middle of a storm, and asks whether you would like to stand in it together.

choices.text: Stand in the storm with {him}

mem.note: stood in the storm with me

effects.log: Lightning walks over both of you for an hour. Afterwards your hair stands on end for a week, and {npc} calls on you every day of it.

choices.text: Watch from the gatehouse

mem.note: watched the storm from the gatehouse

effects.log: {npc} stands in the storm alone, and comes in soaked and a little disappointed.

choices.text: Call down a bolt of your own

mem.note: called down a bolt of its own on the gate

effects.log: Your bolt splits the cloud above the gate. The whole house comes out to see, and {npc} pretends not to be impressed.

events.text: In the healing halls of the Jade Lotus House, {npc} takes your wrist to read your pulse before saying a word, and keeps hold of it a little longer than a healer needs to.

choices.text: Let {him} read everything, the dark too

mem.note: let me read its whole heart

effects.log: "There is a demon in here," {he} says quietly. "There is in everyone. Yours is smaller than you think."

choices.text: Take your hand back

mem.note: took its hand back

effects.log: {He} lets go at once and apologises. The rest of the visit is very polite.

choices.text: Ask to read {his} pulse in return

mem.note: read my pulse in return

effects.log: Under your fingers {his} pulse is far too fast for a healer of ten thousand years. Neither of you mentions it.

events.text: You meet {npc} in the Queen Mother's peach garden, where the trees fruit once every three thousand years. One peach is ripe. There are two of you.

choices.text: Give {him} the peach

mem.note: gave me the only ripe peach

effects.log: {He} cuts it in two with a fingernail and gives you half, as if that had always been the plan.

choices.text: Wait three thousand years for the next one together

mem.note: offered to wait for the next peach with me

effects.log: "That is the most romantic thing anyone has said to me," {npc} says, "and also very impractical."

choices.text: Leave it for someone who needs it more

mem.note: left the peach on the tree

effects.log: A gardener finds it the next day and takes it to a dying immortal of the lower isles. {npc} hears of it and says nothing, but remembers.

events.text: {npc} takes you riding on the back of a cloud whale, out past the last isle where the sky turns dark blue and the stars come close enough to touch.

choices.text: Touch one

mem.note: touched a star with me

effects.log: It is cold, and hums. {npc} laughs at your face for the rest of the ride.

choices.text: Ask {him} what {he} was before the clouds

mem.note: asked what I was before

effects.log: {He} tells you about a fishing village and a drowned brother. Nobody has asked {him} in four thousand years.

choices.text: Fall asleep on the whale's back

mem.note: fell asleep on the cloud whale

effects.log: You wake with {npc}'s cloak over you and the whale circling home.

events.text: A game of Go with {npc} turns, over three days, into the first real quarrel between you, about a stone you swear you did not move.

choices.text: Admit you moved it

mem.note: admitted moving the stone

effects.log: {npc} is so surprised by the honesty that {he} forgets to be angry.

choices.text: Insist you did not

mem.note: swore it never moved the stone

effects.log: The quarrel lasts a month. The board stays exactly where you left it, and in the end {npc} comes back to finish the game.

choices.text: Sweep the stones off the board and start again

mem.note: swept the board clean

effects.log: You both start again from nothing. It is a better game.

events.text: The eldest of {npc}'s house, an immortal so old {his} name is carved on the Jade Court's first pillar, summons you, alone, to explain why {npc} should waste {his} time on you.

choices.text: Answer with your deeds

mem.note: stood up to our eldest

effects.log: The elder listens to all of it without blinking, and then says, "Adequate." The Jade Court hears that you were called adequate, which from that one is praise.

choices.text: Answer that it is not the elder's time to waste

mem.note: told our eldest it was my choice

effects.log: A terrible silence. Then the elder laughs, for the first time in an age, and {npc} hears of it before you are home.

choices.text: Bow, and say you have no answer yet

effects.log: The elder dismisses you with a wave. The court gossips that you were found wanting, and you spend a long time thinking about why.

events.text: {npc} gives you a gift wrapped in silk: a single star, small as a pearl, taken from a sky that ended a hundred thousand years ago. {He} will not say what it cost.

choices.text: Wear it always

mem.note: wears my star always

effects.log: You wear it on a cord at your throat. In the dark it lights the way, very faintly.

choices.text: Give {him} something of yours in return

mem.note: gave me something of its own

effects.log: You give {him} the oldest thing you own, from a life below. {He} holds it as if it were the star.

choices.text: Ask what it cost

mem.note: asked what my gift cost

effects.log: "A great deal," {he} says, and changes the subject, and you wish you had not asked.

events.text: Late one night {npc} asks you what you remember of the world below: not the battles, the little things. The smell of rain on a road. A street market. Someone's laugh.

choices.text: Tell {him} about the little things

mem.note: told me the little things of the world below

effects.log: You talk until dawn about bread, and rain, and old songs. {npc} listens like someone very thirsty.

choices.text: Say you have let it all go

mem.note: said it remembers nothing below

effects.log: {npc} looks sad, and says that {he} used to say that too.

choices.text: Take {him} to look down through the clouds

mem.note: showed me the world below

effects.log: You part the clouds over a small town at night. {npc} watches the lights for an hour without speaking.

events.text: On the night after the wedding the cranes of the isle will not settle. They fly in rings above the hall until dawn, and {npc} says that in {his} house that means the marriage will outlast the sky.

choices.text: Stay up and watch them with {npc}

mem.note: watched the cranes with me

effects.log: At dawn the cranes come down all at once onto the roof, and you both laugh.

choices.text: Ask what it means if they settle early

mem.note: asked about the cranes

effects.log: "Nobody knows," {npc} says. "They never have."

events.text: Your first real quarrel as a married pair: {npc} thinks you look down at the world below far too often, and that it is not good for an immortal to keep one foot in the dust.

choices.text: Say the world below made you who you are

mem.note: stood up for the world below

effects.log: {npc} is quiet for a long while, and then asks you to show {him} where you were born.

choices.text: Promise to look down less

mem.note: promised to look down less

effects.log: You keep the promise for nearly a decade, which above the clouds is no time at all.

choices.text: Ask what {he} left below, that {he} will not look at

mem.note: asked what I left below

effects.log: It is the right question. {He} does not answer it for a year, and then {he} does, all at once.

events.text: A year after the wedding you and {npc} build a house of your own on a small floating isle: one hall, one garden, one pine tree older than the dynasty below.

choices.text: Plant a peach tree beside the pine

mem.note: planted a peach tree at our house

effects.log: It will fruit in three thousand years. You both intend to be there.

choices.text: Carve both names over the door

mem.note: carved our names over the door

effects.log: Visitors from the Jade Court stop to read it. It becomes a small landmark.

choices.text: Leave the door uncarved, for the names to come

mem.note: left the door for the names to come

effects.log: {npc} understands at once, and blushes, which an immortal of {his} age is not supposed to be able to do.

events.text: When {npc} gives a first cry above the clouds, it rains in the world below, warm and gentle, over six provinces. The farmers call it a lucky year. They will never know why.

choices.text: Hold the newborn up to see the clouds

effects.log: The child stops crying and stares at the sky as if it were an old friend.

choices.text: Look down at the rain

effects.log: Somewhere below, a child of your old line is dancing in it. You are sure of it.

events.text: {npc} grabs your finger with a tiny hand, and a thread of qi as fine as silk runs up your arm. A newborn should not be able to do that. Above the clouds, it seems, they can.

choices.text: Let the qi run, and feel what it is

effects.log: It is your own qi, and the other parent's, and something new that is neither. The child yawns.

choices.text: Gently take your finger back

effects.log: The child protests at length. The whole isle hears about it.

events.text: The star-readers of the Jade Court come uninvited to read {npc}'s fate, as they do for every child born above the clouds. They argue all night over the charts.

choices.text: Send them away: the child's fate is the child's

effects.log: The star-readers leave offended. The court talks of your rudeness. The child sleeps through all of it.

choices.text: Let them read, and listen

effects.log: They say the child will climb high and quarrel with heaven once. The Jade Court is pleased to have been consulted.

events.text: The hall of your clan is finished on its isle: white jade, a single long room, and an ancestral altar with nothing on it yet. Your heirs stand along the walls, waiting to see what you will put there.

choices.text: Put nothing on it: let the clan earn its ancestors

effects.log: The altar stays bare. Your heirs understand, slowly, that it is theirs to fill.

choices.text: Put the first weapon you ever held

effects.log: A plain thing from the world below, on an altar of jade. Every visitor asks about it.

choices.text: Put a handful of earth from the world below

effects.log: A little dust on white jade. The clan will never forget where it came from.

events.text: The Jade Court sends a herald with the seal of your clan, and a list of the duties a clan above the clouds owes heaven: tribute, a seat in the council of houses, and silence about the world below.

choices.text: Accept every duty

effects.log: The herald bows very low. The clan has a seat at the council from this day.

choices.text: Accept, except the silence about the world below

effects.log: The herald writes it down with a pained face. The first thing you do is look down at your line below.

choices.text: Accept the seal, and send the list back unread

effects.log: The court is scandalised for a decade. The other young houses think it is magnificent.

events.text: {npc}, of your blood, comes to you with a request: to go down to the world below for a mortal lifetime, the way you once lived, and see what the clan is made of.

choices.text: Give {him} your blessing

mem.note: let me go below

effects.log: {He} comes back eighty years later, quieter and older in the eyes, and is the wisest of the clan from that day.

choices.text: Forbid it: the clan needs {him} here

mem.note: kept me above the clouds

effects.log: {npc} obeys. The Jade Court approves. You are not sure you do.

choices.text: Go down with {him} for a season

mem.note: walked the world below with me

effects.log: A season in the world below, two immortals pretending to be travellers. You both remember it for ten thousand years.

events.text: {npc}, of your blood, has quarrelled with an heir of a great house at the Jade Court, and the other house demands an apology or a duel.

choices.text: Make {him} apologise

mem.note: made me apologise

effects.log: The apology is stiff and correct. The great house is mollified. {npc} does not speak to you for a year.

choices.text: Let {him} fight the duel

mem.note: let me fight my own duel

ok.log: {npc} wins, narrowly, and the clan's name is spoken with new respect.

mem.note: let me fight my own duel

fail.log: {npc} loses, and is hurt, and the clan is laughed at for a season.

choices.text: Go to the other house yourself, and settle it

mem.note: settled my quarrel for me

effects.log: Over tea the two elders agree the young are impossible. It is the start of a long friendship between the houses.

events.text: {npc} is at the gate of the next realm and afraid of it. {He} asks you to sit outside the door while {he} tries.

choices.text: Sit outside the door

mem.note: sat outside my door at the gate

effects.log: Three days. On the third night the door opens and {npc} walks out changed, and sits down beside you, and cannot stop smiling.

choices.text: Go in with {him}, and guide the qi

mem.note: guided my qi at the gate

effects.log: It is harder with two. It works. {npc} will always wonder whether {he} could have done it alone.

choices.text: Tell {him} to face it alone, as you did

mem.note: sent me to the gate alone

effects.log: {He} goes in alone and comes out alone. {He} does not ask you for anything again for a long time.

events.text: A great house of the Jade Court proposes a match for {npc}, of your blood: an alliance that would double the clan's standing. {npc} has never met the one proposed.

choices.text: Accept the alliance

mem.note: married me off for standing

effects.log: The wedding is magnificent. {npc} is polite to everyone, all evening, and looks at you once.

choices.text: Leave it to {npc} to decide

mem.note: let me choose for myself

effects.log: {npc} meets the proposed match three times, and then chooses someone else entirely. The great house sulks. The clan is happier.

choices.text: Refuse on {his} behalf

mem.note: refused a match for me

effects.log: The great house is insulted and says so at court. {npc} thanks you privately, and very warmly.

events.text: The council of houses meets once a century, and your clan has a seat at the far end of the table, next to a draught. An older house suggests, politely, that a young clan should listen and not speak.

choices.text: Listen, for this century

effects.log: You listen to forty days of argument without a word. The old houses decide you have manners. Next century the seat is nearer the fire.

choices.text: Speak anyway

effects.log: You say what the young houses have all been thinking. The old houses never forgive it, and the young houses never forget it.

events.text: Someone has left an offering on the clan's ancestral altar in the night: a rice cake, a wooden toy and a letter, sent up through the clouds by a temple below where a child of your old line prays.

choices.text: Answer the prayer

effects.log: You read the letter twice. Whatever heaven says about meddling, you look down that night.

choices.text: Keep the letter, and leave it at that

effects.log: You keep the letter in your sleeve for a thousand years. It is the most valuable thing the clan owns.

events.text: The clan's steward reports that the clan is poor for a house above the clouds: one hall, a garden, and debts to the Vermilion Phoenix House for the jade.

choices.text: Pay the debt from your own purse

effects.log: The Vermilion Phoenix House is paid in full, which surprises it. The clan stands a little taller at court.

choices.text: Let the clan be poor and proud

effects.log: The clan learns to mend its own roof. It is good for them.

choices.text: Send the heirs to hunt treasures on the far isles

effects.log: They come back after a century with half a treasure and a great many stories. The debt waits.

events.text: Through the clouds you watch {npc}, of your own blood, grow grey over what feels to you like an afternoon. {He} sits in a doorway below and looks up at the sky, the way you taught {him} to, long ago.

choices.text: Send a breeze down to {him}

mem.note: sent a breeze down to me from the sky

effects.log: The breeze lifts {his} hair. {He} smiles, and says something to the sky you cannot hear.

choices.text: Only watch

effects.log: You watch until {he} goes inside. It is enough, and it is not enough, and that is how it is.

events.text: You see {npc}, of your blood, in trouble below: a debt, a powerful enemy, a house about to be lost. Heaven's rule is that the world below is not yours to arrange.

choices.text: Reach down anyway, just this once

mem.note: sent a miracle when I needed it

effects.log: A lost deed turns up, an enemy changes their mind, and the house is saved. A censor of the Jade Court notes it in a very small hand.

choices.text: Keep heaven's rule, and grieve

effects.log: You watch {him} lose the house and find another, smaller one. People below are very good at that.

events.text: {npc}, a descendant of your line who has never heard your name, has opened a martial school below and hung an old sword over the door. You know that sword. It used to be yours.

choices.text: Make the sword hum once, when {he} is alone

effects.log: {He} stares at it for a long time, and then bows to it, for no reason {he} could explain.

choices.text: Leave it be

effects.log: The sword is in good hands. You find you are proud of someone who does not know you exist.

events.text: A wedding below: {npc}, of your line, many generations down, marrying in a village you once rode through. Nobody there remembers you. The family keeps a story about an ancestor who went up into the sky.

choices.text: Send a rain of petals

effects.log: Petals fall from a clear sky all through the feast. The village talks of nothing else for a generation, and the Jade Court of nothing else for a week.

choices.text: Only watch, and raise a cup

effects.log: You raise a cup above the clouds as they raise theirs below. Nobody sees it. That is all right.

events.text: {npc}, a descendant of your line, is a scholar below, writing a history of the great masters. {He} has reached your chapter, and {he} is getting most of it wrong.

choices.text: Send {him} a dream with the truth in it

effects.log: {He} wakes and rewrites the chapter by lamplight. It is still a little wrong, in a way you rather like.

choices.text: Let the history be wrong

effects.log: In {his} history you are taller and kinder and die nobly. It is a good story. You decide not to spoil it.

events.text: A delegation in robes you have never seen, and know, waits for you on the cloud road: the elders of the clan a past life of yours founded above the clouds. They have kept your hall swept for all the years you were gone, and they would know your soul anywhere.

choices.text: Take up the clan again

effects.log: They lead you to the hall, and the ancestral altar, and the first name carved on it, which was yours.

choices.text: Bless them, and walk on as who you are now

effects.log: The eldest bows very low and says the hall will wait. Halls above the clouds are good at waiting.

events.text: At the Jade Court a young immortal stops in front of you, stares, and runs. An hour later the whole of the clan your past life founded is waiting outside your door, in silence, with the ancestral tablet held between them.

choices.text: Open the door and take the tablet

effects.log: The tablet is warm in your hands. Behind you the clan rises from its knees, and it is your clan again.

choices.text: Ask them to let the old name rest

effects.log: They are quiet a long time, and then the eldest says, "Then we will keep it for you." And they go.
